sentences.text:
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Revenue Lko And 6 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Durgendra Kumar Tiwari

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Sarvesh Kumar Dubey
Hon'ble Mrs. Sangeeta Chandra,J.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Standing Counsel for the State Respondents
and Ms. Samidha, Advocate, who has filed her vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party no.2, which
is taken on record.
2.

This writ petition has been filed with the following main prayers:-
Ramdei And 5 Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Revenue ... on 10 September, 2024
Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the opp.

Parties concerned to take the necessary action regarding the grievance of the petitioners raised in their application contained in Annexure no. 1 to this writ petition and also provide the fair and proper compensation of the land gata no. 960 min, area 0.051 hectare situated in village Bighapur Kala Tehsil Bighapur District Unnao of petitioners to petitioners of non agricultural land of category 143 Z.A. and L.R. Act in place of agricultural land in the interest of justice.
ii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the opp.
Parties concerned to consider and decide the application of the petitioners as contained in Annexure No. 1 to this writ petition expeditiously within the stipulated time as provided by this Hon'ble court in interest of justice."
3. Learned counsel appearing for the opposite party no. 2 has raised a preliminary objection regarding the maintainability of the writ petition on the ground that the petitioners have statutory remedy under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 before the Arbitrator as the petitioners are mainly aggrieved by the amount of compensation that has been determined by the Competent Authority Land Acquisition.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has placed reliance upon an order passed by this Court in Writ-C No. 4128 of 2024, 'Mahesh Kumar Vs. State of U.P.', where a similar prayer has been made as in this writ petition and it was disposed of by this Court on 13.05.2024 with a direction to the petitioner to make an application to the Competent Authority under the National Highways Act within a period of two weeks and the respondent no. 4 was directed to decide the same in accordance with law within a period of twelve weeks, thereafter.

entities.text: Mahesh Kumar Vs. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The dispute with regard to the said writ petition related to apportionment of compensation and the writ petitioner was directed to approach the Competent Authority Land Acquisition.

5. In the case of the petitioners, however, the petitioners have disputed the amount of compensation as given by the award of the Competent Authority Land Acquisition for which the petitioners have statutory remedy of approaching the Arbitrator under Section 3(G)5 of the National Highways Act,
1956 6.
Accordingly, this writ petition stands disposed of.
